# shadergx

> Render a fragment shader and inspect the pixels: black, constant, NaN output, unused uniforms. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes the rendered image as evidence.

shadergx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. An agent writes a
fragment shader it cannot see; `shadergx inspect` renders it headlessly
(moderngl + EGL) and reports what is wrong with the pixels.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/shadergx" shadergx --help
uv tool install ./packages/shadergx      # from a clone
```

Needs Python 3.10+, moderngl, numpy, Pillow and a GL context (Mesa/EGL or a GPU).

## Use

```sh
shadergx inspect shader.py            # render + report + storyboard, exit 1 on any error
shadergx inspect shader.py --json
shadergx inspect shader.py --no-storyboard
shadergx render  shader.py -o shader.png
```

A shader file defines `shader` (a `Shader`) or module-level `FRAGMENT` /
`UNIFORMS` / `SIZE` / `TIME`. The wrapper supplies `#version`, the vertex
shader, `uv`, `u_resolution`, `u_time` and `fragColor`.

## Checks

error: `compile-error`, `bad-size`, `nan-output`, `black-output` (mean
RGB/alpha below 0.02).
warn: `constant-output`, `uniform-unused`.
info: `nondeterministic`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
